name: Radish

companions.note: Compatible spacing and timing; radishes break soil surface, spinach fills in beneath
Radishes repel flea beetles that target brassicas; harvest before kale needs the space

pnw_notes: One of the fastest crops in the garden — ready in 3–4 weeks. Best in cool weather; heat makes them pithy and bolt quickly. Classic trick: sow radishes to mark rows of slow-germinating crops like carrots, then harvest as the slower crop fills in. Succession sow every 2 weeks from March through May and again August through October for continuous harvest.

frost_hardiness.notes: Root is protected in soil. Tops may die back in a hard freeze — just pull the root. Harvest before ground freezes solid.

planting_windows.notes: Sow thickly, thin to 3 in; harvest before heat arrives
Fall window — cool temps produce best flavor and texture
Spring harvest; pull before they crack or go pithy in summer heat
Fall harvest; flavor peaks with cool nights
